summary: Three-tier token model (primitive, semantic, component) with tier purposes, sample CSS per tier, dark mode as semantic override, naming pattern, categories, file layout, flat-token migration, DTCG JSON shape.
mech: Primitives hold raw values only; semantic tokens may reference only primitives; component tokens reference semantic tokens; verify no component rule points at a raw value or primitive.
Implement dark mode as a block that overrides only semantic tokens; primitives and component tokens stay unchanged; verify the dark block contains no new raw values.
Name tokens category-item-variant-state; migrate flat per-component hex tokens by extracting primitives, aliasing semantics, then pointing component tokens at semantics.

summary: Sample primitive scales: gray and one brand hue ramps 50-950, status hues, 4px-based spacing ramp, type size, leading, weight and tracking scales, radius, shadow, duration and z-index ladders.
mech: Build every scale as a stepped ramp on one base unit (spacing on 4px steps); verify each spacing value used in output is a ramp member.
Define named z-index layers in ascending order dropdown, sticky, modal, popover, tooltip so overlay stacking is predictable; verify no ad hoc z-index numbers.
Alias motion durations as fast, normal, slow from a raw duration ramp so components cite intent, not milliseconds.

summary: Semantic color roles paired with foreground counterparts (surface, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, status, border, ring), spacing, type and interaction aliases, dark overrides, good-versus-bad usage example.
mech: Give every fill role a paired foreground token (primary and primary-foreground); verify each pair meets contrast in both light and dark themes.
Component styles must use semantic roles, never primitives directly; flag any component rule citing a raw ramp step such as gray-50.
Dark theme overrides surfaces, muted, secondary, accent, border and input roles only; brand and status roles keep values unless contrast fails.

summary: Component-tier token sets for button, input, card, badge, alert, dialog and table, each aliasing semantic roles for variant fills, hover and active, focus, error, disabled, sizing and shape.
mech: For each component list tokens per variant and per state (bg, fg, hover-bg, active-bg, border) aliased to semantic roles; verify every declared state has a token.
Input tokens must cover placeholder, focus border and ring, error border and text, disabled fill and text; a missing one means an unspecified state.
Size variants (sm, default, lg) change only padding, height and font tokens; colors stay shared so variants never fork the palette.

summary: Interactive state table with triggers, state precedence order, transition timings, focus-ring spec, disabled, loading and error treatments, variant patterns via local custom properties, contrast minima, ARIA markup.
mech: When states overlap resolve by precedence disabled > loading > active > focus > hover > default; verify each interactive component documents all six.
Focus ring is a two-layer outline (background-colored offset then ring color) on focus-visible; error state swaps ring to error color; verify ring contrast at least 3:1.
Never signal state by color alone: add icon or text; error text sits below field with icon, clears on valid input; loading sets aria-busy plus screen-reader text.

summary: Spec tables for button, input, card, badge, alert, dialog and table: variants with use cases, size ladders, per-state treatments, anatomy sketches, dialog widths, table alignment and row densities.
mech: Map button variants to action rank: filled for primary, tonal for secondary, outline or ghost for tertiary, link for navigation, destructive only for dangerous actions.
Table cells: left-align text, right-align numbers and row actions, center status badges; offer compact, default and comfortable row heights.
Dialog anatomy: header with title and close, scrollable content, footer actions with cancel before confirm; dialog goes full width minus margins on mobile.

summary: Maps semantic tokens to a utility-CSS framework: space-separated HSL variables for light and dark, config color mapping, radius derived from one variable, component classes, duration tokens, dark toggle.
mech: Conflict: this file stores colours as space-separated HSL channels in an old-style config file; the stack table forbids those legacy snippets and maps variables through the theme layer.
Method still valid: one central variable per semantic role, light and dark blocks, radius steps derived from one base radius, filled-button hover as same role at lower opacity.
Initialize dark mode from the system colour-scheme preference, then toggle a root class; verify against the installed framework major version before porting.

summary: Sixteen named aesthetic direction recipes (color seed ranges, type family, shape and depth, signature, imagery, do-not-use contexts), three design dials with presets, per-direction motion envelopes; all self-labelled unverified.
mech: Direction = color seed ranges, type family, radius and depth, one signature, imagery, do-not-use contexts; when adapting, change at least two fields and write why.
Check each direction's do-not-use list against the product (trust finance or health, weak phones, long text, children, elderly); any match vetoes it; one direction per product.
Set three 1-10 dials (variance, motion, density) from the product; density picks the spacing range; scale motion duration by distance, element size and task importance.

summary: Visual heuristics by screen archetype with exception-note format, first-glance check, hero weight, color proportion, restraint budget, card discipline, conditional dark mode, scaled motion, identity templates, anti-generic audit.
mech: Classify screen archetype first; hero and color-proportion rules apply only to showcase screens; skipping a rule needs a one-line exception: rule, evidence-backed reason, substitute.
Restraint budget per screen: one gradient, one blur layer, one focal animation, one accent hue, four type sizes, three weights; delete any effect whose removal loses nothing.
A redesign counts as distinct only with written change in two of typography, layout composition, component relationships, beyond surface color, shadow or radius.

summary: Visual token set with may-use and may-not-use rules per token (color roles, type scale, spacing, elevation, radius, motion, breakpoints), component recipes with states, presentation plan, palette table, per-screen blueprint templates.
mech: Every token carries a may-use and may-not-use rule; components cite token names only, raw hex appears once in a palette table with measured contrast and evidence label.
Text roles: primary, secondary and meaningful tertiary text at least 4.5:1 against their surface; non-text cues 3:1; disabled text carries a one-line reason; never below 12px.
Per-screen blueprint: archetype and anchor, one row per element listing tier and tokens plus hit area, hero clearance, all states, reflow at three widths and largest font.

summary: Four-step Devanagari verification (glyph coverage by family and build, explicit fallback stack, five render checks, honest evidence label), companion font list, subset snapshot table, general type rules.
mech: Never infer script support from a font name: check the exact build's Unicode block and shaping tables, else add an explicit script fallback to the stack.
Render real mixed strings and check conjuncts, vowel signs, line height 1.5-1.6 body, clipping inside buttons, chips and inputs, and mixed-script baseline; unrendered means not-tested.
Mobile body at least 16px, nothing under 12px, line 35-60 characters mobile and 60-75 desktop, tabular numerals for data; no negative tracking, caps or italics on Devanagari.

summary: Table of 74 named heading and body font pairings with mood keywords and best-for contexts, including per-script pairings, prefaced by a warning not to assume Devanagari support from font names.
mech: Pairing choice is keyword matching: product context and mood words against each pairing's mood and best-for columns; at most two families; single-family pairings rely on weight contrast.
Non-Latin scripts get script-native families; 'subset not listed in snapshot' means unverified, not absent; run a coverage check and add a fallback before using.
Pairing logic contrasts a display face (serif, geometric or condensed) with a neutral readable body face; trust or accessibility contexts favour hyperlegible or plain sans.

summary: Matrix of 50 named visual styles, each with suitable contexts and do-not-use contexts, plus a short selection method; points to supplemental and deprecated styles in the full table.
mech: Pick a style from product type, audience and task; then check its do-not-use list; any accessibility or performance veto removes it; one style across the whole product.
Recurring vetoes: effect-heavy styles (glass, 3D, motion-led, neumorphic) excluded for accessibility-critical, low-end devices, dense data; loud styles excluded for finance, health, government.
Platform design systems fit only products living on that platform; using one elsewhere imports conventions users will not expect.

summary: Motion durations scaled by distance, element size and task importance, web motion tiers with easings, performance and accessibility rules, and a chart picker mapping data shape to chart with thresholds.
mech: Scale duration by distance, size and importance (press about 100ms, sheet 300-450ms, one hero moment per screen); animate transform and opacity only; exit 60-70% of enter.
Animations must be interruptible and never block input; reduced-motion turns entrances and shimmer static; motion never outranks accessibility, frame budget or task clarity.
Pick chart by data question; fallbacks: under 4 points a stat card, over 15 categories a table, over 5 slices a bar; add table, insight line, non-color encoding.

summary: Table of 192 product categories each mapped to a page pattern, two priority styles, colour mood, typography mood, key effects and an avoid list; rendered from the reasoning table.
mech: Category drives five choices: page pattern, style pair, colour mood, type mood, effects; the avoid column vetoes trust-breaking looks (playful in finance, neon or heavy motion in health).
Avoid lists also name missing function (hidden fees, no search, no status, color-only indicators); port these as functional veto checks, not visual picks.
Conflicts with style-matrix: low-contrast soft styles prescribed for health and calm categories that style-matrix vetoes for critical accessibility; check style vetoes after lookup.

summary: Worked examples: placement before decoration, literal versus rethought layouts for two sample product requests, a micro-change answer format, a missing-reference gate with resume line, honest evidence-label wording.
mech: Place the primary action where the thumb reaches (bottom, full width, 48-56px) before styling; a well-styled element in the wrong place still fails.
For a request listing N separate tools, compare literal (N pages), rethought (one workspace with auto-detect plus one-tap override) and zero-step options; pick with reasons.
Evidence wording: claim tool-verified only with the command shown; without a render run the verdict is spec-approved, render-unverified; never say passed or approved.

summary: Version history of the source skill from v11 to v18 rev 3: audit fixes, architecture split, size router, scorecard layers, evidence labels, verify-first script rule, and historical untested-status notes.
mech: Recompute every tool-cited number in examples by re-running the tool; the source found its own 'verified' contrast example wrong this way.
Keep untested status explicit: the source states the method was never field-tested on a real requirements document.

summary: 32 mobile-app UX rules (accessibility, forms, touch, navigation, feedback, performance, animation, type, safe areas, theming) each with description, do, don't, good and bad code, severity.
mech: Each row is a checkable do/don't with severity; audit a mobile screen by walking rows and citing violated issue plus severity, critical first.
Verify icon-only buttons and inputs expose accessible labels, targets meet minimum size and spacing, every gesture action has a visible button alternative, modals offer escape.
Forms: validate on blur or submit not per keystroke, correct keyboard type, next-field focus, password reveal, allow paste and password managers; respect safe areas and reduced motion.

summary: 25 data-shape rows mapping to best and secondary chart types with when-to-use, when-not, volume thresholds, colour guidance, accessibility risk, notes, fallback, library, interaction level.
mech: Choose chart from the data question, then test its when-not column (too few points, too many series or categories) and switch to the named fallback.
Volume thresholds pick rendering: vector graphics for small sets, canvas plus downsampling above about a thousand points, aggregate beyond; source's own numbers.
Every chart needs non-color encoding (line styles, patterns, direct labels), a visible data table plus summary, and keyboard focus that reveals hover values.

summary: 192 product-type rows each prescribing a full semantic palette in hex (primary, secondary, accent with on-colours, background, foreground, card, muted, border, destructive, ring) plus a mood note.
mech: A palette is a set of semantic roles each with a paired on-colour; derive roles from mood and category, then check every pair's contrast before use.
When an accent fails contrast against its on-colour, darken it and record the original value; the table notes 56 such adjustments.
Variety risk: about half the primaries fall in blue hues and one blue plus one violet recur across 33 rows; table-driven palettes converge.

summary: 105 curated icons from one outline icon library, each with category, keywords, import and usage code, best-for, style, semantic role and allowed contexts, plus one icon-accessibility guideline row.
mech: Classify icon role: decorative beside visible text is hidden from assistive tech; meaningful alone needs a text alternative; inside a control, the control needs name and state.
One icon family and one stroke style per surface; prefer the most semantically precise glyph, use a second library only as a consistent fallback.
Pick list itself is single-library lock-in with fixed size and weight; port the role and context rules, not the icon names.

summary: 34 landing-page patterns, each with keywords, section order, primary call-to-action placement, colour strategy, recommended effects, conversion notes, pattern id and aliases used for matching.
mech: Landing pattern = ordered sections plus where the primary action repeats (hero, then after proof or at bottom); choose by what visitors must believe before acting.
Conversion notes carry checks: action label contrast at least 4.5:1 on its fill, skip option for immersive intros, label live data as live only with a real source.
Aliases map category wording to pattern ids so a generator can join product rows to section templates; this join makes pages structurally alike.

summary: 17 motion rows for hover, scroll reveal, stagger, page transition, parallax, skeleton and carousel at subtle, standard, complex tiers, with trigger, duration, easing, code snippet, do, don't, performance notes.
mech: Pick motion tier by intent (subtle, standard, complex) and keep hover displacement under about 2px; animate only transform and opacity; never layout properties.
Auto-rotating content needs visible pause, previous and next controls, stops on focus, hover, offscreen or hidden tab, and clears timers on cleanup.
Split-text and scroll-linked effects only on short headlines; restore original text for assistive tech; reduced motion gets the static final state.

summary: 192 product types with keywords, primary and secondary style picks, landing pattern, dashboard style, colour focus and key functional considerations; the main lookup table for generating a system.
mech: Keyword match a product description to a product row, which then joins to style, landing pattern, dashboard style and colour rows; the row is the generator's seed.
Key considerations column lists functional must-haves per category (map-centric layout, fare estimate, seat map); port as a prompt to list category-critical features.
Convergence: one minimal style is primary in 75 of 192 rows; table-driven style picks will look alike.

summary: 44 component-framework performance rules (async waterfalls, bundle size, server, client, rerender, rendering, JS performance, advanced) each with description, do, don't, good and bad code, severity.
mech: Audit by walking critical rows first: start independent fetches in parallel, defer awaits into the branch that needs them, avoid barrel imports, lazy-load heavy modules.
Rerender rules: functional state updates, derive values instead of syncing state, memoize only expensive work, read latest values via refs synced after commit.

summary: 88 named visual styles (50 active, 29 supplemental, 9 deprecated) with colours, effects, best-for, do-not-use, mode support, performance cost, accessibility risk, checklist, CSS variables, ids, aliases, replacements.
mech: Style reasoning columns: best-for and do-not-use contexts, performance cost with drivers (blur, animation, 3D), accessibility risk; veto high-cost or high-risk styles for weak devices or critical users.
Every style row carries a pass checklist; port the idea of a per-direction checklist that must include measured text contrast, keyboard, visible focus, reduced motion.
Lifecycle columns (active, supplemental, deprecated with replacement id) let a generator retire stale presets instead of serving them.

summary: 74 heading and body font pairings with category (serif plus sans and so on), mood keywords, best-for contexts, hosted font URL, CSS import, framework config and short rationale notes.
mech: Pairing justification is contrast of roles: an expressive heading face (serif, display, condensed) against a calm readable body face; single-family pairs rely on weight steps.
Match by mood and best-for keywords; load only weights actually used and use a swap display strategy; verify non-Latin script coverage separately.
Convergence: one neutral sans appears in 12 pairings and sans-plus-sans is the largest category; table picks drift to the same look.

summary: 192 product categories with pattern, style priority, colour mood, type mood, key effects, JSON decision rules (must-have and conditional constraints), anti-patterns, severity, and sparse reasoning with confidence scores.
mech: Decision rules are condition-to-override JSON: must-have constraints plus conditionals (if trust needed, if mobile, if low performance, if conversion focused) that swap style or add constraints.
Port the mechanism: list category must-haves, then apply context conditions (device, trust, data density, audience) that override the default look; record which fired.
Only 31 of 192 rows carry reasoning text; confidence scores are self-assigned and unverifiable; treat picks as starting points.

summary: 119 UX rules across navigation, motion, layout, touch, interaction states, accessibility, performance, forms, responsive, typography, content, feedback, AI and spatial UI, each with do, don't, code and severity.
mech: Audit checklist: walk rows by severity; each gives a do, a don't and a good versus bad code sample, so violations are citable with issue name.
Newer rows encode current accessibility criteria: focus not obscured, dragging alternatives, minimum target size, accessible authentication, redundant entry, consistent help, focusable error summary.
Compact-control rules: long tokens wrap, essential text never truncated, chip groups reflow before shrinking, live badges announce politely, transitions cancellable with state set directly.

summary: Standard permissive open-source licence text granting reuse of the upstream dataset and code with copyright notice retained.

Catalog manifest: schema version, verification date, record counts per table (styles by status, products, palettes, fonts, icons, guidelines, stacks), snapshot hashes, font promotion policy, pending font candidates.

summary: 51 provenance records for reasoning rows, dataset contracts, styles and snapshots, each with source file and key, status, verified date, review SLA, scope, confidence and cited sources.

Dataset contracts state boundaries honestly: the palette table does not attest that every colour pair was measured; recheck contrast before use.

summary: Licence inventory for 1934 hosted font families (name, licence type, date added, designers, status, verified date) from a pinned upstream revision, plus 8 excluded families with reasons.

Font search can rank by keywords, category and popularity; popularity ranking pushes every output toward the same few families.

summary: Upstream icon library dump: package and version, six weights, 1512 icons each with name, component, codepoint, categories, tags, version info and import lines; 100 curated entries validated.

summary: 50 version-pinned guidelines for a web component framework (components, performance, routing, state, forms, testing, styling, architecture) with do, don't, code samples, severity, docs link, status, verified date.

Rows carry an applies-to version and verified date; confirm the project's installed version matches before citing a rule.

summary: 53 guidelines for a content-first static site framework: islands architecture, zero client JS default, content collections with schemas, static paths, view transitions, SEO, integrations, with severity and docs.

Structured content uses typed collection schemas with required fields; known dynamic routes are generated at build, not fetched at runtime.

mech: Reserve image space with aspect ratio or dimensions to prevent layout shift; use documented z-index tokens; responsive widths per breakpoint, never one fixed desktop width.
Never remove focus outlines without a visible ring replacement; bounded decorative animation with a reduced-motion override.

summary: 75 guidelines for a desktop Java UI toolkit: theming, controls, architecture, markup loading, layout, accessibility, threading, CSS, binding, performance, testing, tables, with severity and version.

summary: 60 guidelines for a React meta-framework: routing, caching, rendering, data fetching, images, middleware, API, performance, fonts, metadata, environment, links, pinned to a current version.

Route-level error boundaries with a reset action instead of scattered try/catch.

summary: 76 guidelines for a Vue component library: installation, overlays, navigation, components, icons, theming, tables, layout, dashboard, feedback, colour mode, forms, with severity and version.
mech: Configure brand colours once in central app config and theme tokens; never hardcode colours inside components; wrap the app once in the library root provider.

summary: 67 guidelines for a Vue meta-framework: data fetching, state, routing, server routes, rendering, lifecycle, SEO, middleware, error handling, links, environment, auto-imports, with severity.

summary: 51 guidelines for a cross-platform native app framework: styling, lists, performance, components, navigation, state, images, forms, touch, animation, async, accessibility, with severity.
mech: Virtualized lists with stable key extraction and memoized row renderers for long data; handle hardware back on focused screens; avoid inline style objects.

summary: 66 guidelines for a component UI library: components, forms, state, rendering, hooks, performance, effects, props, accessibility, typing, events, context; two legacy rows marked deprecated.
mech: Derive values during render instead of storing them; effects only for external sync, with cleanup and complete dependency lists; stable ids as list keys, never indexes.

summary: 68 guidelines for a copy-in component registry: setup, forms, components, registry, theming, dialogs, toasts, sidebar, charts, accessibility, patterns, sheets, with severity and CLI version.

Use a dialog for modal content and forms, an alert dialog only for interrupting confirmations; install components through the registry CLI, not stale copies.

summary: 55 guidelines for a compiled UI framework and its app framework: reactivity, stores, props, events, lifecycle, logic, bindings, slots, styling, transitions, actions; 11 legacy-mode rows deprecated.

summary: Small CLI that looks up font families in the bundled font snapshot and reports whether a Devanagari subset is listed, suggests near names and companion fonts; informational exit code.

summary: Small CLI computing contrast ratio for colour pairs, with optional foreground alpha composited over the background, reporting pass or fail at 4.5, 3 and 7 to 1.
mech: Safety scan: 0 hits (pure arithmetic).
Algorithm: composite foreground alpha over opaque background, linearize sRGB channels, luminance 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B, ratio (lighter+0.05)/(darker+0.05); compare to 4.5, 3, 7.
Gap: always exits 0 even on failure and ignores background alpha; a gate version should return non-zero on failure.

summary: BM25 search engine over the data tables and per-stack tables: synonyms, stopwords, domain detection, per-domain score floors and coverage thresholds, stack version and legacy filtering.

summary: Generator that composes a full design-system recommendation from the tables: product match, reasoning rules, multi-domain search, mode resolution, palette, type, effects, dials, and optional persisted master and page files.

Pipeline: match product category, load its decision rules, apply dials, search style, colour, type, landing, effects; pick best by priority keywords; resolve light or dark; choose agreeing palette.
Mode coherence: resolve light or dark first, then palette and anti-patterns must agree; derived dark surfaces are fixed slate values, so every dark output looks alike.

summary: Closed, non-executable grammar for decision rules: a fixed set of condition names triggered by whole-word signals in the query, and four validated action prefixes.
mech: Safety scan: 0 hits; rules are parsed as data, never evaluated as code.

mech: Safety scan: 0 hits; persistence flags can write files under a chosen output directory, skipping existing master files unless forced.

mech: Safety scan: 0 hits (reads files, prints pass or fail).

Recompute any numeric result quoted in examples by running the tool; fail on mismatch. States plainly it proves structure only, not design quality.

summary: Data-integrity validator for all tables: required columns, duplicate keys, JSON rules, palette pair contrast, cross-table references, font, icon and catalog hashes, provenance freshness, stack version contracts.
mech: Safety scan: 1 hit, a URL-parsing import; no network calls found by the scan.

Provenance gate: manual-verified status cannot rest on derived sources only; each record needs a valid date, freshness SLA and resolvable source key.
